title: DSA Zero to Hero in Python
description: Comprehensive 16-week DSA curriculum for Python developers. Part 3 covers 1D Dynamic Programming, 2D Grid & String DP, and Grind 75 Timed Mock Interviews.
goal: Master dynamic programming and pass timed technical interview simulations.
subject: Data Structures & Algorithms
audience: Software engineering intern and new-grad candidates learning DSA in Python.

modules.title: 1D Dynamic Programming & State Transitions
modules.summary: Overlapping subproblems, optimal substructure, 1D memoization vs tabulation.

modules.title: 2D Dynamic Programming & Grid Paths
modules.summary: Grid path DP, 0/1 Knapsack state matrices, string LCS/Edit Distance.

modules.title: Grind 75 Timed Mocks & Interview Readiness
modules.summary: Timed mock interview practice, strategy review, and complex edge case validation.

tasks.title: Dynamic Programming Principles & Memoization
tasks.description: Study Dynamic Programming core principles: overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure. Compare top-down recursion with memoization (lru_cache) against bottom-up iterative tabulation. Derive subproblem DAG state transitions.
objectives: Identify overlapping subproblems in recursive decision trees
Implement top-down memoization using Python functools.lru_cache
Build bottom-up 1D DP tabulation arrays with optimal space complexity
tradeoffs: Top-down memoization only computes required states but incurs call stack overhead; bottom-up tabulation computes all table states iteratively with fast array indexing
verificationQuestions: What two conditions must a problem satisfy for Dynamic Programming to apply?
How does bottom-up tabulation eliminate recursion call stack space?

tasks.title: Climbing Stairs
tasks.description: Solve Climbing Stairs in Python using Fibonacci state transitions dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2] optimized to O(1) space.

tasks.title: Min Cost Climbing Stairs
tasks.description: Compute minimum step costs using DP transition cost[i] += min(cost[i+1], cost[i+2]) in Python.

tasks.title: House Robber
tasks.description: Solve House Robber using state decision rob = max(dont_rob_prev + num, rob_prev) in Python.

tasks.title: Coin Change
tasks.description: Solve Unbounded Knapsack Coin Change using bottom-up tabulation array dp[i] = min(dp[i], 1 + dp[i - coin]) in Python.

tasks.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
tasks.description: Find LIS using O(n^2) DP tabulation or optimize to O(n log n) using binary search (bisect_left) patience sorting in Python.

tasks.title: Word Break
tasks.description: Determine if string can be segmented into dictionary words using boolean DP array dp[i] checking valid word substrings.

tasks.title: 2D Grid DP & String Subsequence Matrices
tasks.description: Study 2D Dynamic Programming matrix formulations. Master grid path counting dp[r][c] = dp[r-1][c] + dp[r][c-1], 0/1 Knapsack matrix states, and string subsequence alignment tables (LCS).
objectives: Formulate 2D state matrices for grid traversal and string matching
Differentiate 0/1 Knapsack (bounded) from Unbounded Knapsack transitions
Optimize 2D matrix space to 1D rolling rows
tradeoffs: 2D DP matrices provide clean visual state transitions, but storing full m x n tables requires O(m*n) space which can often be reduced to O(n) using 1D rolling rows
verificationQuestions: How do you transition state in a grid DP when moving only right and down?
Why does 0/1 Knapsack require iterating backwards when space-optimized to 1D?

tasks.title: Unique Paths
tasks.description: Calculate unique grid paths from top-left to bottom-right using 2D DP tabulation or space-optimized 1D row in Python.

tasks.title: Longest Common Subsequence
tasks.description: Compute LCS length of two strings using 2D matrix state transitions dp[i][j] = 1 + dp[i+1][j+1] if match else max(dp[i+1][j], dp[i][j+1]).

tasks.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Cooldown
tasks.description: Model stock trading state transitions (Buying, Selling, Cooldown) using state machine DP in Python.

practice.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Cooldown

tasks.title: Target Sum
tasks.description: Transform Target Sum into 0/1 Subset Sum DP partition problem solved via 2D memoization or 1D hash map state counting.

tasks.title: Edit Distance
tasks.description: Compute minimum Levenshtein edit operations (insert, delete, replace) to convert word1 to word2 using 2D DP matrix.

tasks.title: Grind 75 Timed Mock Session 1 (Arrays & Strings)
tasks.description: Solve 2 Medium problems under 45-minute timed constraints using the Grind 75 tool interface. Speak thought process aloud, state Big-O bounds before coding, and test edge cases.

tasks.title: Grind 75 Timed Mock Session 2 (Trees & BFS/DFS)
tasks.description: Solve 2 Medium Tree/Graph problems under timed constraints. Focus on clean recursion syntax, handling null root nodes, and graph visited set edge checks.

tasks.title: Grind 75 Timed Mock Session 3 (Heap & Backtracking)
tasks.description: Solve 2 Medium Heap/Backtracking problems under 45-minute timed simulation. Verify state undoing and time complexity explanations.

tasks.title: Grind 75 Timed Mock Session 4 (Dynamic Programming)
tasks.description: Solve 2 Medium Dynamic Programming problems under timed conditions. Write out state definitions and base cases on paper prior to writing code.

tasks.title: Tech Interview Cheatsheets & Edge Case Audit
tasks.description: Review Tech Interview Handbook algorithms cheatsheet. Memorize standard edge cases: empty array, single element, negative numbers, integer overflow bounds, duplicate keys, cyclic graphs, and disjoint components.
objectives: Audit universal coding interview edge cases
Review time and space complexity summary tables
Master STAR methodology for behavioral interview questions
verificationQuestions: What edge cases should you always test before declaring your code complete?
How do you explain trade-offs if an interviewer asks for better space complexity?
